title: post-merge hook reads only commit subjects, so body-trailer "Closes SH-NN" never auto-closes

description:
## What

The managed `post-merge` hook auto-closes stories referenced by
`closes|fixes|resolves SH-NN`, but it only reads commit **subject lines**. Any
such reference written conventionally — in the commit body, as a trailer — is
invisible to it, so the story is never closed.

## Where

`src/hooks.rs`, `POST_MERGE_HOOK`:

    git log --format='%s' "$ORIG_HEAD..HEAD" 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r msg; do
      echo "$msg" | grep -oiE '(closes?|fixes?|resolves?)\s+[A-Z]+-[0-9]+' | ...

`%s` is the subject alone. `%B` is the raw body including the subject.

## Why it breaks

Conventional Commits — which `CLAUDE.md` mandates for this repo — put the
closing reference in a trailer, not the summary line. The subject is reserved
for a concise description under 72 characters. So the hook's trigger and the
project's own commit style are mutually exclusive in practice: following the
style guide guarantees the hook does nothing.

## Extent

Reproduced on the merge of PR #54 (merge commit 84b64e1), whose branch commit
carried a `Closes SH-55` trailer:

    $ git log --format='%s' ORIG_HEAD..HEAD | grep -oiE '(closes?|fixes?|resolves?)\s+[A-Z]+-[0-9]+'
    (no output — nothing closed)

    $ git log --format='%B' ORIG_HEAD..HEAD | grep -oiE '(closes?|fixes?|resolves?)\s+[A-Z]+-[0-9]+'
    Closes SH-55

SH-55 remained `todo` after the merge and had to be closed by hand.

Corroborating history: `0aa0094`/`d08af8e` include a commit titled
`chore(storyhook): close SH-45 as done` — a manual close. The feature has
plausibly never worked for a body-trailer reference, and the workaround
(closing by hand in a follow-up commit) has become the de-facto process.

## Repro

1. `story hooks install`
2. On a branch, commit with the reference in the body:

       git commit -m "fix(x): something" -m "Closes SH-N"

3. Merge to main.

Expect SH-N to still be OPEN.

## Last known good

None known. The `%s` format is present in the hook's original definition, so
this likely never worked for body trailers.

## Fix

Change `--format='%s'` to `--format='%B'` in `POST_MERGE_HOOK`.

Note `%B` emits multi-line records, so the surrounding `while IFS= read -r msg`
loop no longer receives one commit per iteration. It does not need to: the
loop's only job is to feed text to `grep -oiE`, which is line-oriented and
already emits one match per line. Piping `git log --format='%B'` straight into
the existing `grep -oiE ... | while read match` is simpler and correct. Verify
that a commit mentioning two stories closes both.

## Preventative action

The defect class is "hook logic shipped as an untested string literal."
`POST_MERGE_HOOK` is a `&str` in `src/hooks.rs` with no coverage — nothing
executes it. The plugin suite (`plugin/claude-code/tests/`) demonstrates the
pattern for testing real shell behavior against the real binary; an equivalent
test that installs the hook into a scratch repo, merges a branch whose commit
body closes a story, and asserts the story went to `done` would have caught
this and will catch the next hook regression.
